gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the invalid claim that a nonzero homogeneous whole-line solution belongs to the stated global L2 weak-solution class. The prediction also supplies the corresponding local-interval or propagator repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The whole-line extension of nonzero norm-conserving homogeneous data is only locally square-integrable, not in L2(R,H), so it cannot satisfy the old global weak-solution definition; the extension-based proof step is therefore invalid.

component_coverage.gold_component: The asserted whole-line homogeneous solution has constant nonzero norm and is in L2_loc but not L2(R,H), invalidating its use as the defined weak solution and the extension step.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-005 explicitly identifies the global L2 requirement, norm conservation for nonzero homogeneous data, failure of the whole-line weak-solution claim, and a repair using bounded-interval weak solutions or the propagator formulation.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 diagnoses an invalid test-function inclusion and admissibility gap in the S-star converse. It does not identify the distinct spectral-cutoff residual mismatch between time mollification and the spectral projection, nor the resulting unsupported convergence in X_H.
